name: ASSAY OFFICE, RECORDS ROOM
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE REGISTER OF ASSAYS
LOOK_AT: Every ounce of color ever brought in, weighed and named. Nineteen names, twelve years. It is a shorter book than the town believes.
Nine years of assays, in a hand that has not varied once. Not one crossing-out.
The columns are ruled by hand, every page, every year. She has never once bought ruled paper.
LISTEN_TO: Pages. Very few of them turn.
Nothing.
A page lifting in the draft from the door and lying down again exactly where it was.

subjects.name: THE NINETEEN NAMES
LOOK_AT: The nineteen. Some are dead, some left, one runs the bakehouse now. Not one of them found enough to matter, and every one of them is famous for it.
Each name has a date beside it, and the dates are spread across twelve years like a slow leak.
I have read them often enough to know any of them if I met him. I am not going to meet most of them.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Fame this size is very quiet.
Nothing. Nineteen men, filed quietly.
Nothing. A short list keeps a long silence.

overrides.TALK_TO: I read them aloud once, quietly. It felt like a roll call. Nobody answered, which is the point of the list.

subjects.name: THE SAMPLE SHELF
LOOK_AT: Rows of little bottles, each holding a pinch of the territory. Labeled in a hand that gets smaller as the years go on.
Every sample assayed in nine years, in labeled vials. It is beautiful, in the way that only a completed thing is beautiful.
There are gaps where bottles were taken out and never returned. Some men took their pinch home to remember it by.
LISTEN_TO: Glass, shoulder to shoulder. A faint ring when the floor moves.
Nothing. It is nine years of work and it is not asking for anything.
The ring again, very faint, as I step back. Glass, sorry to see me go.

overrides.PICK_UP: Every bottle is somebody's whole year. I am not qualified to hold a year.

subjects.name: THE CRUCIBLE
LOOK_AT: The crucible that has judged every hope in the district. It is the size of a teacup and twice as final.
Its inside is glazed by fire to a dull gold that has nothing to do with gold.
Tongs hang beside it, long enough to keep a hand well away from the truth.
LISTEN_TO: Cold. A crucible only speaks at temperature.
Nothing. It is waiting for a fire and a question.
A faint tick as it settles on its stand. Even cold, it has weight.

overrides.USE: Cold, and not mine to fire. Some instruments you earn.

subjects.name: THE SCALES CABINET
LOOK_AT: The good scales, behind glass, level to a hair. The one instrument in Consolation nobody has ever accused of anything.
The glass door has a brass lock. The key, I am told, is on a ribbon round her neck.
Beside the scales, a set of weights in a velvet tray, each in its own hollow, none missing.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing at all. Precision resting.
Nothing. Precision does not hum.
The glass door ticking very slightly in its frame when the street door goes.

overrides.OPEN: Locked, and the key is Winnie, and Winnie is the lock.

subjects.name: THE MAP OF CLAIMS
LOOK_AT: The district in pencil, each claim a small rectangle of intention. Mine is there. It is drawn slightly crooked, which feels personal.
The claims along the creek are drawn in a careful hand, the ones up the hill in a quicker one, as if the town got ahead of her.
Claim One is drawn in ink and labeled. Every other claim is pencil.
LISTEN_TO: Paper on a damp wall, easing.
A pin working loose somewhere in the damp.
Nothing. The district, flat and quiet, the way it never is.

subjects.name: THE STOOL
LOOK_AT: A high stool worn by the assayer's particular way of sitting, which is mostly leaning.
One leg has been mended with wire. She mended it herself, by the look of the wire.
It stands exactly where the window light falls on the ledger. Not an inch to the left.
LISTEN_TO: One loose joint. It announces him.
The loose joint again, when I set a hand on it. It is used to one weight only.
Nothing. It is waiting for her.

overrides.USE: I sat on it. It announced me. I got down.

subjects.name: THE ACID BOTTLES
LOOK_AT: Aqua fortis, in brown glass, with a stopper the shape of regret. It tells gold from everything that wishes it were.
Each bottle carries a printed label, POISON, and beneath it, in her hand: ALSO TRUTH.
One drop has eaten into the bench, a small brown crater. It was a test somebody failed.
LISTEN_TO: A hiss so small it may be memory.
A tiny ping of glass as the shelf takes the weight of the morning.
Nothing. It does its work in silence, and I respect that more than I can say.

subjects.name: THE FILED CERTIFICATES
LOOK_AT: Certificates of assay, filed by year. The folders get thinner toward the present, like the town is holding its breath.
Each certificate is stamped, signed and dated, and most of them say nothing worth stamping.
The folders are tied with tape, and every bow is the same size.
LISTEN_TO: Paper, in quantity. A dry sea.
Nothing. Certainty, in folders, makes no sound.
Paper settling in a drawer, a long, dry exhale.

subjects.name: THE BACK WINDOW
LOOK_AT: It looks up the diggings. From here you can watch men carry hope in and results out.
It is set high, so nobody passing can see in. She can see out only by standing on the stool.
From up here the diggings look like a page of arithmetic, and none of it adds up.
LISTEN_TO: Picks, far off. The hills, being asked.
A pick, then another, then a man laughing at something that was probably not funny.
The wind across the glass, come down from the diggings with nothing in its hands.

subjects.name: THE STAIN ON THE FLOOR
LOOK_AT: An old acid burn, scrubbed at for years and settled into the grain. Some result somebody took badly.
Someone has laid a mat over the edge of it. The mat is not quite big enough.
It is the shape of a hand, if you look at it the wrong way, which I did.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Whatever happened here is finished happening.
Nothing. The floor has forgiven it.
Nothing. Even the boards around it are quiet.

subjects.name: THE STOVE
LOOK_AT: A small stove, lit low, with a kettle on it and a pan of something that might be supper or might be glue.
The fender is polished. Everything in this room is looked after, and the stove is looked after twice.
Her shawl is drying on the rail. She works here, and lives a good part of the rest of the time here too.
LISTEN_TO: A low ticking, like a clock that has been told to keep its voice down.
The kettle, thinking about it.
Coals shifting, settling, staying in.

subjects.name: THE COT IN THE CORNER
LOOK_AT: A cot. Used. She has slept in this building, and recently, and more than once.
One blanket, folded square, and a pillow with the shape of a head still in it.
From it you can see the street door. She sleeps facing the way she might be needed.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. It is very carefully not being slept in, just now.
A spring easing in the frame, long after anyone sat on it.

subjects.name: THE SPARE APRON
LOOK_AT: A spare apron on a peg, starched and pressed, with acid holes along the hem in a neat row.
The pocket holds a pencil sharpened at one end only, which in this town is a sign of good character.
It matches the one she is wearing, stain for stain. She keeps a spare of everything except time.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Linen, on a peg.
The peg creaking very slightly when the door opens.
Nothing. It is ready for tomorrow, and the day after.

subjects.name: THE SHELF OF REFERENCE VOLUMES
LOOK_AT: Assaying manuals, a chemistry, a German dictionary and the territorial statutes, all with their spines broken in the right places.
One manual is annotated in her hand. In three places she has corrected the author.
The German dictionary is the most used. I cannot think what for, and I am afraid to ask.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Knowledge, resting.
A spine creaking as the shelf takes the damp.
Nothing. They have been read thoroughly and have nothing new to say.

subjects.name: HER TEA THINGS
LOOK_AT: A cup, a saucer, a tin of tea and a spoon, arranged on a tray as exactly as everything else she keeps.
One cup. She does not entertain.
The tin's label is from Canton by way of San Francisco by way of Sheng. Even her tea has a paper trail.
LISTEN_TO: A faint clink of spoon on saucer as the floor moves.
Nothing. The cup is clean and dry and upside down.
Nothing. Tea for one makes the smallest sound in the world.
